sections.text: About I build Android apps at ███████████████████, focused on community features — plus the unglamorous work that decides whether an app feels fast: a customizable payment library on Google Play Billing, a resource controller that made dynamic lists behave, liveness, and macro-benchmarking of UI-layer resource use. I measure before I believe. When an existing tool could not answer a question, I wrote the harness: an inspector for WebSocket traffic, and a benchmark for how coding agents decide what to read. Both started as side projects and ended up changing how I work. This site is built the same way. Each project is an exploded view of how it is actually put together — layer by layer, component by component, with the numbers that came out of the measurements. Kotlin · Compose · Coroutines · Room · Clean architecture · Android profiling · Firebase · CI/CD

visibleTexts: A portfolio rendered as exploded architecture: real layers, real components, real numbers — no stock photos, no invented metrics.
Scarlet Inspector — Every WebSocket frame, captured and inspectable.
Every WebSocket frame, captured and inspectable.

I build Android apps at ███████████████████, focused on community features — plus the unglamorous work that decides whether an app feels fast: a customizable payment library on Google Play Billing, a resource controller that made dynamic lists behave, liveness, and macro-benchmarking of UI-layer resource use.

I measure before I believe. When an existing tool could not answer a question, I wrote the harness: an inspector for WebSocket traffic, and a benchmark for how coding agents decide what to read. Both started as side projects and ended up changing how I work.
This site is built the same way. Each project is an exploded view of how it is actually put together — layer by layer, component by component, with the numbers that came out of the measurements.
Kotlin · Compose · Coroutines · Room · Clean architecture · Android profiling · Firebase · CI/CD
Built with Next.js, three.js and a lot of measurement. Source on GitHub.

Each project is an exploded view of how it is actually put together — layer by layer, component by component, with the numbers that came out of the measurements.
